_note: Lipad Pinas destination highlights, keyed by destination ICAO. tag = one punchy sentence for the hook; offers = 2 spoken-friendly lines (what the destination offers / popular in the area). Number-light, long-lasting facts only; re-check before adding new places.

CYVR.tag: Mountains, ocean and a big city skyline, all in one place.
offers: Vancouver sits between the mountains and the Pacific, and it is known for Stanley Park, Granville Island and the seawall walk around the city.
Whistler's ski slopes are a day trip away, and the city is loved for its fresh seafood and its mix of food from around the world.

KJFK.tag: The city that never sleeps is waiting.
offers: New York City is home to Times Square, Central Park, the Statue of Liberty and the Brooklyn Bridge.
It is also famous for its Broadway shows, world class museums and food from every corner of the world.
Los Angeles is home to Hollywood, the Walk of Fame, Santa Monica Pier and miles of sunny beaches.
Theme parks like Disneyland and Universal Studios are within easy reach, along with the Griffith Observatory and its views of the city.

KSFO.tag: Golden Gate views and cable car rides.
offers: San Francisco is famous for the Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz Island and its historic cable cars.
Fisherman's Wharf and Chinatown are favorite stops, and the wine country of Napa Valley is a short drive away.

OEJN.tag: The gateway to the Red Sea and the holy cities.
offers: Jeddah is the gateway for pilgrims heading to Makkah and Madinah, and its Al Balad old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Red Sea corniche, the King Fahd Fountain and some of the best diving and snorkeling in the region are right on its coast.

OERK.tag: Saudi Arabia's capital, where heritage meets skyscrapers.
offers: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia, with the Kingdom Centre tower and the historic Diriyah, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Visitors enjoy the Edge of the World cliffs outside the city, desert adventures, and a fast growing food and entertainment scene.

OMAA.tag: Home of a magnificent white marble mosque.
offers: Abu Dhabi is home to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, one of the largest mosques in the world, and the Louvre Abu Dhabi museum.
Yas Island has Ferrari World and more theme parks, and the beaches of Saadiyat Island are a favorite way to relax.

OMDB.tag: Skyscrapers, desert safaris and the tallest tower in the world.
offers: Dubai is home to the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world, and the huge Dubai Mall.
Visitors enjoy desert safaris, the Palm Jumeirah, the gold and spice souks, and some of the best shopping anywhere.

OTHH.tag: A modern skyline beside the Arabian Gulf.
offers: Doha is known for the Museum of Islamic Art, the traditional Souq Waqif market and the futuristic skyline of West Bay.
Katara Cultural Village and the Corniche walk by the Gulf are favorite stops, and the city hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup.

RCTP.tag: Night markets, hot springs and Taipei 101.
offers: Taipei is famous for its night markets and street food, like beef noodle soup and bubble tea, which began in Taiwan.
Taipei 101, the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and the hot springs of Beitou are favorite stops, and the lantern lined streets of Jiufen are a short ride away.

RJAA.tag: Neon lights, sushi and centuries old temples.
offers: Tokyo mixes ultra modern districts like Shibuya and Shinjuku with calm temples like Senso-ji in Asakusa.
Visitors love the sushi and ramen, the anime shops of Akihabara, Tokyo Disneyland, and views of Mount Fuji on clear days.

RJTT.tag: Neon lights, sushi and centuries old temples.
offers: Tokyo mixes ultra modern districts like Shibuya and Shinjuku with calm temples like Senso-ji in Asakusa.
Visitors love the sushi and ramen, the anime shops of Akihabara, Tokyo Disneyland, and views of Mount Fuji on clear days.
Osaka is famous for its street food, especially takoyaki and okonomiyaki, around the bright Dotonbori canal.
Osaka Castle and Universal Studios Japan are top attractions, and Kyoto and Nara are an easy train ride away.
Seoul blends royal palaces like Gyeongbokgung with the shopping streets of Myeongdong and the youth culture of Hongdae.
It is famous for Korean barbecue, street food, K-pop and K-dramas, and N Seoul Tower gives a view over the whole city.

RPLC.tag: Pampanga's gateway to adventure and great food.
offers: Clark is in Pampanga, known as the culinary capital of the Philippines, famous for sisig and its home cooking.
Visitors enjoy the annual hot air balloon festival, treks to nearby Mount Pinatubo, and the shopping and nightlife of Angeles City.

RPLL.tag: The capital with centuries of history.
offers: Manila is the capital of the Philippines, with the walled city of Intramuros, Rizal Park and the historic Manila Cathedral.
Visitors enjoy the sunset at Manila Bay, the food crawl in Binondo, one of the oldest Chinatowns in the world, and the malls and nightlife of Makati and Bonifacio Global City.

RPMD.tag: Home of the king of fruits and the highest mountain in the country.
offers: Davao is known for the durian, the king of fruits, and Mount Apo, the highest mountain in the Philippines.
Visitors enjoy the Philippine Eagle Center and the beaches of Samal Island, just a short boat ride away.

RPVI.tag: A heritage city with a famous bowl of noodles.
offers: Iloilo is known for its Spanish colonial churches, like Miagao Church, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its grand old mansions.
The Iloilo River Esplanade, the Dinagyang Festival and the local batchoy noodle soup are highlights, and the sweet mangoes of Guimaras are nearby.

RPVK.tag: The gateway to Boracay and the Ati-Atihan Festival.
offers: Kalibo is a gateway to Boracay, famous for the powdery white sand of White Beach.
Kalibo also hosts the Ati-Atihan Festival every January, one of the most colorful festivals in the Philippines.

RPVM.tag: The Queen City of the South.
offers: Cebu is home to Magellan's Cross, the Basilica del Santo Nino and the famous Cebu lechon.
Visitors swim with whale sharks in Oslob, go canyoneering at Kawasan Falls in Badian, and island hop around Mactan and Bantayan.
Puerto Princesa is the gateway to the Puerto Princesa Underground River, one of the New Seven Wonders of Nature.
Honda Bay island hopping, firefly watching along the Iwahig River and fresh seafood in the city are favorites, and El Nido and Coron are further north.

VHHH.tag: A dazzling skyline, dim sum and Disneyland.
offers: Hong Kong is famous for Victoria Harbour, the Peak Tram and the nightly harbour light show.
Visitors enjoy dim sum, Hong Kong Disneyland, the giant Tian Tan Buddha on Lantau Island and the street markets of Mong Kok.

VTBS.tag: Golden temples, street food and shopping.
offers: Bangkok is famous for its glittering temples like Wat Arun and the Grand Palace, and Wat Pho's giant reclining Buddha.
Street food, floating markets, rooftop bars and huge shopping malls make it a favorite stop, and the beaches of Pattaya are a short drive away.

VVTS.tag: Motorbikes, coffee and incredible street food.
offers: Ho Chi Minh City is famous for its pho and banh mi, and for Vietnamese iced coffee on busy street corners.
Highlights include the Notre Dame Cathedral, Ben Thanh Market and the War Remnants Museum, with day trips to the Mekong Delta and the Cu Chi Tunnels.
Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia, with the National Monument, the Old Town of Kota Tua and the Istiqlal Mosque, one of the largest mosques in Southeast Asia.
Visitors enjoy its food and huge malls, and the Thousand Islands offshore make an easy beach escape.

WMKK.tag: Twin towers, street food and shopping.
offers: Kuala Lumpur is home to the Petronas Twin Towers, once the tallest buildings in the world, and the KL Tower.
Visitors enjoy the Batu Caves, the street food of Jalan Alor, Merdeka Square and affordable shopping in Bukit Bintang.
Singapore is famous for Gardens by the Bay and its Supertrees, Marina Bay Sands and the Merlion.
Visitors enjoy hawker food like chicken rice, Sentosa Island, the Night Safari and Universal Studios, and the city is clean and easy to get around.
Sydney is home to the Opera House and the Harbour Bridge, with the famous Bondi Beach just a short ride from the center.
Visitors enjoy the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk, Taronga Zoo, the Royal Botanic Garden and day trips to the Blue Mountains.
Guangzhou is the home of Cantonese cuisine and dim sum, with a morning tea culture that locals call yum cha.
Visitors enjoy the Canton Tower, the colonial buildings of Shamian Island and the Chen Clan Ancestral Hall.

ZSPD.tag: A futuristic skyline beside the Bund.
offers: Shanghai is famous for the Bund waterfront and the futuristic Pudong skyline with the Oriental Pearl Tower.
Visitors enjoy Yu Garden, shopping on Nanjing Road, xiaolongbao soup dumplings, and the high speed Maglev train from the airport.

RPLI.tag: Ilocos' gateway to sand dunes and heritage.
offers: Laoag is the gateway to Ilocos Norte, with Paoay Church, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the Bangui Windmills.
The La Paz sand dunes, with sandboarding and 4x4 rides, and Ilocos favorites like empanada and bagnet are top stops.

RPME.tag: One of the oldest settlements in the country.
offers: Butuan is one of the oldest settlements in the Philippines, where ancient wooden boats called balanghai were discovered along the Agusan River.
The Butuan National Museum shows these treasures, and the Agusan Marsh Wildlife Sanctuary, a vast wetland full of birds, is within reach.

RPMG.tag: The Orchid City of the Philippines.
offers: Dipolog is called the Orchid City of the Philippines, and it is known for sunset views along its boulevard by the sea.
Dakak Beach Resort, and the Rizal Shrine in nearby Dapitan, where national hero Jose Rizal lived in exile, are favorite stops.

RPMR.tag: The marble capital of the Philippines.
offers: Romblon is known as the marble capital of the Philippines, with marble sculptures and souvenirs found across the province.
Visitors enjoy quiet beaches and clear waters, and hikers head for Mount Guiting-Guiting on nearby Sibuyan Island.

RPMV.tag: The white water rafting capital of the Philippines.
offers: Cagayan de Oro is known as the white water rafting capital of the Philippines, with rapids on the Cagayan River.
Visitors enjoy Macahambus Cave, the Gardens of Malasag and the ziplines of Dahilayan, and the city is a gateway to Camiguin Island.

RPMZ.tag: Asia's Latin City, where Spanish flavor still lives.
offers: Zamboanga City is known as Asia's Latin City, because of Chavacano, a local language based on Spanish.
Visitors enjoy Fort Pilar, the pink sand of Santa Cruz Island and the colorful vinta sailboats that cross the bay.

RPNS.tag: The surfing capital of the Philippines.
offers: Siargao is the surfing capital of the Philippines, famous for the Cloud 9 wave in General Luna.
Visitors enjoy island hopping to Naked, Daku and Guyam islands, the Sugba Lagoon and the Magpupungko tide pools.
Bohol is famous for the Chocolate Hills, over a thousand grass covered hills that turn brown in the dry season.
Visitors meet the tiny tarsier, cruise the Loboc River, and relax on the white sand of Alona Beach in Panglao.

RPUT.tag: The gateway to caves, beaches and the Cagayan Valley.
offers: Tuguegarao is the gateway to the Cagayan Valley, with Callao Cave in Penablanca, which has a chapel inside a limestone cavern.
It is also known for pancit batil patong, the local noodle dish, and the beaches of Santa Ana are a few hours north.

RPVA.tag: Home of the longest bridge in the country.
offers: Tacloban is home to the San Juanico Bridge, the longest bridge in the Philippines, linking Leyte and Samar.
Visitors see the Santo Nino Shrine and the MacArthur Landing Memorial in nearby Palo, and taste local treats like binagol.
Bacolod is known as the City of Smiles, and it hosts the colorful MassKara Festival every October.
Visitors enjoy chicken inasal, sweet piaya and napoleones, the Ruins in Talisay, an old sugar mansion, and the heritage houses of Negros.
Dumaguete is known as the City of Gentle People, with a relaxed seaside promenade along Rizal Boulevard.
It is the gateway to Apo Island, where you can snorkel with sea turtles, and the famous sansrival cake is a must try.
Caticlan is the jump off point to Boracay, just a short boat ride away.
Boracay is famous for the powdery white sand of White Beach, spectacular sunsets, island hopping, diving and parasailing.
